blk_part_01_part_1_first_nations_continu.text: One key word is Country. In the First Nations sense, Country is a living relationship with land, water, and the wider living world. It is not only a place on a map. Welcome to Country and Acknowledgement of Country ceremonies show that this idea still shapes public life in cities such as Sydney and Melbourne. Torres Strait Islander peoples also keep strong sea and island links across the Torres Strait, north of Queensland.

blk_part_05_part_5_mateship_friendly_man.text: Because mateship values equals, manners often feel informal to visitors. People may use first names quickly and get to the point in ordinary talk. Direct talk usually means saying the main idea without long ceremony. Visitors who expect more formal openings can find Australian talk sudden at first, then clear and warm once the friendship pattern shows.

blk_part_06_part_6_shared_stories_visito.text: Anzac Day is on 25 April. It remembers the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps, or ANZAC, who landed at Gallipoli in 1915, and later service by Australian forces. Dawn services at war memorials, marches in towns and cities, and quiet morning gatherings give the day a shared national shape.
